definition: ChatGPT Space is a shared workspace inside ChatGPT, announced at DevDay 2026, where teammates, ChatGPT, and always-on agents (dots) work together on the same projects. Think of it as a shared drive folder crossed with a chatroom: documents, slides, and spreadsheets live in one place, and both humans and agents can open, edit, and comment on them. OpenAI is also shipping ChatGPT-native apps for documents, slides, and spreadsheets to live inside it.

edges.label: agents as coworkers
edges.note: A Space treats agents as collaborators on shared work, not just tools you prompt.

edges.label: shared agents need rules
edges.note: When people and agents edit the same workspace, the rules about what each may touch matter more.

example.body: Your team is building a product-launch deck in a Space. You draft the outline; your dot pulls the latest metrics from the analytics app and drops fresh charts into the slides overnight; a teammate edits the messaging in the morning. Nobody emailed files around or wondered which version was current. The deck just evolved — with a history of who, or what, changed each slide.

name: ChatGPT Space
tagline: A shared workspace where teammates, ChatGPT, and always-on agents work on the same project together.
whyItMatters: This is OpenAI's bid to make ChatGPT the place work happens, not just the place you ask questions. The moment agents share your workspace — seeing your drafts, editing your slides — collaboration gets faster, and the question of who changed what (and what each party is allowed to touch) gets more important.
